evidence: Caes. BG 1.25: scūtum manū ēmittere et nūdō corpore pugnāre (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 10.36.8: ēlige, cum cīve an hoste pugnāre mālīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of single fighters and of armies. The opponent with cum and the ablative, or with in or adversum and the accusative; what one fights for with prō: prō commodīs patriae (Cic. Inv. 1.1, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: scūtum manū ēmittere et nūdō corpore pugnāre
phrases.english: to let the shield drop from the hand and fight with the body unprotected

phrases.latin: ēlige, cum cīve an hoste pugnāre mālīs
phrases.english: choose whether you would rather fight a fellow citizen or an enemy

sources: Lewis & Short: pugno
